editorial.headline: Dental Adhesive Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20234 covers dental adhesive manufacturing, open nationally across all business scales with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20234 is a narrow industrial classification: the manufacture of dental adhesive products. The record does not expand the category into clinical services, dental practice, retail distribution, or medical-device trading. Its center of gravity is production. That makes the activity easier to read than many broader manufacturing labels: it is about making adhesive products used in dentistry, not about operating the professional dental setting in which those products may later be used.

At the national level, the record is open. Its PMA status is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. The business scales open to the activity are also broad: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar**. In plain English, the national line says that this activity can be registered across the full scale spectrum recorded here, and that a foreign-owned company is not capped below full ownership by the national figure supplied in the record.

Bali changes the practical answer completely. The Bali-side status is **Blocked (risk class)**, and the record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true. The reason is explicit: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026**. The moratorium rule attached to the record is equally direct: **Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)**. So the honest reading is not “open with a Bali caveat”; it is open nationally, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali moratorium information provided.

That distinction matters because the record contains two different regulatory pictures, not one blended answer. Nationally, KBLI 20234 reads as a foreign-open manufacturing activity with a 100% ceiling. Locally, for Bali, the same activity is stopped for PMA registration because of the recorded risk-class moratorium. A founder reading this code should therefore keep the two conclusions separate: the national ownership field is permissive, while the Bali registration outcome is blocked by the province-level rule stated in the record.
